name: Shackleton Connecting Ridge
source: NASA Artemis III Candidate Landing Regions (2022) / NASA GSFC LOLA South Pole Data
description: Connecting ridge extending between Shackleton and de Gerlache craters, exhibiting high persistent solar illumination.

name: Peak Near Shackleton
source: NASA Artemis III Candidate Landing Regions (2022) / Mazarico et al. (2011)
description: High ridge near the rim of Shackleton Crater (~0.22 deg from South Pole).

name: de Gerlache Rim 1
source: NASA Artemis III Candidate Landing Regions (2022)
description: Prominent rim crest of de Gerlache crater with favorable Earth line-of-sight.

name: de Gerlache Rim 2
source: NASA Artemis III Candidate Landing Regions (2022)
description: Northern segment of de Gerlache crater rim.

name: Connecting Ridge Extension
source: NASA Artemis III Candidate Landing Regions (2022)
description: Extension of the Shackleton-de Gerlache ridge feature.

name: Malapert Mountain Peak
source: NASA Artemis III Candidate Landing Regions (2022) / Sharpton et al.
description: High massif providing long continuous Earth geometric visibility.

name: Haworth Crater Rim
source: NASA Artemis III Candidate Landing Regions (2022)
description: Elevated rim adjacent to permanently shadowed region in Haworth Crater.

name: Nobile Rim 1 (VIPER Site)
source: NASA VIPER Landing Site Selection (2021) / Colaprete et al.
description: Mountainous rim of Nobile crater characterized by moderate slopes and accessible PSRs.

name: Amundsen Rim
source: NASA Artemis III Candidate Landing Regions (2022)

name: Faustini Rim A
source: NASA Artemis III Candidate Landing Regions (2022)
description: Rim segment between Faustini and Shoemaker craters.

name: Apollo 11 (Statio Tranquillitatis)
source: NASA LROC Apollo 11 Landing Site coordinates / NASA PDS
description: Historical landing site in Mare Tranquillitatis. Equatorial, subject to ~14.75 days unbroken lunar night.

name: Apollo 12 (Oceanus Procellarum)
source: NASA LROC Apollo 12 Landing Site coordinates / NASA PDS
description: Equatorial mare site in Oceanus Procellarum, near Surveyor III.

name: Apollo 17 (Taurus-Littrow)
source: NASA LROC Apollo 17 Landing Site coordinates / NASA PDS

name: Chang'e 4 (Von Kármán)
source: CNSA / Di et al. (2019) Chang'e 4 Landing Site Localization
description: Lunar farside landing site inside Von Kármán crater (South Pole-Aitken Basin). Earth geometric visibility is permanently 0%.
